# Runtime Utilities

`@walmart/ld-kit/utils/*` holds the runtime services this project composes against —
the theme runtime, shared state, the product catalog, and the media / icon /
illustration lookups. They are public library modules: import them by the
subpath shown in their generated `reference/utils/` documentation, call them,
read their generated `.md`.

**Do not memorise this list. Ask for it.** The inventory and every export
signature are generated from the shipped source, so the CLI is always right and
this file cannot go stale:

```bash
node scripts/ld/cli.mjs utils                 # every utility with its one-line intent
node scripts/ld/cli.mjs show <Name>           # full export surface, signatures, types
node scripts/ld/cli.mjs search <keywords>     # find one by what it does, e.g. "product catalog"
```

## Hard Rules

These are the constraints the generated docs cannot express. Everything else
about a utility — what it exports, what each function takes and returns — comes
from `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs show`.

### Product data

- **MUST** source every product from `ProductService` — products, categories,
  hero banners and marketing tiles all come from it. Run
  `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs show ProductService` for the API.
- **Find a real product before you write code**, rather than guessing a SKU:
  `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs products <query>` searches the actual catalog by name or SKU and
  hands back a ready `getProductBySku("...")` call for each hit — the same
  guarantee `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs icons`/`node scripts/ld/cli.mjs illustrations`/`node scripts/ld/cli.mjs media` give you
  below. Run it with no arguments to see the catalog's categories, or
  `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs products <category>` to list every product in one.
- **NEVER** hand-write a product name, SKU, price, image URL, rating or badge as
  an inline literal. Not in pages, not in demos, not in fixtures. Invented
  product data drifts from the catalog and breaks cart consistency and Store
  bindings.
- **NEVER** mock a product as `{ sku: "demo-1", name: "Demo Item" }`. Pick a
  real one: `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs products <query>`, `getProductBySku(...)`, or the first of
  `getAllProducts()`.
- **MUST** guard `getProductBySku` for `undefined` before use — it returns
  `Product | undefined`.
- **MUST** pass Store identity (`{ sku, name, priceCents }`) straight off the
  `Product`, never retyped by hand. See `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs rule component-communication`
  for how those bindings work.
- **NEVER** import `reference/data/productCatalog.json` from app code — it is a
  read-only lookup snapshot for the CLI; use `ProductService`. New products are
  authored upstream in the library catalog.

### Media, icons and illustrations

**Find a name before you write code**, rather than guessing one: `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs icons <query>`, `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs illustrations <query>`, `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs media <query>` search by name across every font/type/tenant (add a bucket — a font key, illustration type, or tenant key — to scope the search; `icons Walmart cart` also accepts a theme name). Run any of them with no arguments to list the buckets. These read the exact same manifests the managers below read at runtime, so the name you find is guaranteed real — the common source of a hallucinated icon or illustration name is skipping this step.

- **MUST** resolve brand media (logos, wordmarks, card art, error states)
  through `mediaManager`, icons through `iconManager`, and illustrations through
  `illustrationManager` / `Illustration`. Each resolves against the **active
  theme**, so a hardcoded asset path or icon name silently breaks every other
  brand. Media tenants also form an inheritance tree and each entry ships
  fully merged, so `getMedia(tenant, name)` already falls back for you — do not
  hand-roll a fallback chain.
- **NEVER** import a manager's backing manifest JSON directly. The manager adds
  theme resolution and tenant inheritance that the raw JSON does not have.
- **NEVER** hand-edit asset metadata in `reference/` or installed library
  assets. Both trees are generated by `npm run airtable:pull-media` /
  `airtable:pull-illustrations` upstream and hand edits are overwritten on the
  next sync. Change the source in Airtable instead.
- **MUST** branch on a media asset's `kind` when rendering — SVG and PNG are not
  interchangeable.
- **MUST** render illustrations with `<Illustration>`, never
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` against the raw SVG string. The component owns
  aspect-ratio, sizing and the accessibility contract.
- **NEVER** inline an SVG that the illustration set already provides, and never
  substitute an emoji or an icon font glyph for an illustration.

Accessibility for these is **binding** — a runtime scanner enforces it (`node scripts/ld/cli.mjs rule a11y`). The one non-obvious part: `<Illustration>` defaults its `aria-label` to the illustration *name*, which is rarely what a user needs to hear — pass a real `title`, or `title=""` for purely decorative use, which also sets `aria-hidden`.

Illustration sizing resolves in this order: `width` + `height` are both used
literally; if only one is given the other derives from the source aspect ratio;
`size` alone applies to the longer source dimension; with none of them it renders
at 100% width with `aspect-ratio` preserved.

### General

- **NEVER** write a parallel helper that re-implements a utility — no second
  product helper, no per-page filtering that duplicates
  `getProductsByCategory`, no local theme map.
- **MUST** check `node scripts/ld/cli.mjs utils` before writing a new helper. The thing you
  need usually already exists in `@walmart/ld-kit/utils/*`.
